title: Understanding Nurse Salary QLD: From Hourly Rate to Annual Pay and Tax
description: Learn how to convert a nurse salary QLD hourly rate to annual pay, including tax, Medicare, and super. Use the 38-hour week formula and see fortnightly estimates.
salarySummary: For a nurse in Queensland earning a hypothetical $45 per hour, working 38 hours a week, the annual gross pay would be approximately $88,920 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I calculate annual pay from an hourly rate for a nurse salary QLD?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a full-time nurse working 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual salary before tax and super. Remember that this assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: What tax and Medicare levy apply to a nurse salary QLD annual figure?
faqs.a: For the 2026–27 financial year, resident tax rates are: nil up to $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% from $45,001 to $135,000; 37% from $135,001 to $190,000; and 45% above $190,000. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. These are deducted from your gross annual pay to estimate take-home pay. Note that HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not included in this estimate.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the nurse salary QLD annual figure?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. So if your annual gross pay is $88,920, your employer would contribute an additional $10,670.40 to your super fund, not included in the annual pay figure shown here.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting an Hourly Nurse Salary QLD to Annual Pay

If you are a nurse in Queensland and you know your hourly rate, you can estimate your annual gross salary using a simple formula. The standard full-time week for most awards is 38 hours, so we use that as the baseline. Multiply your hourly rate by 38 hours per week, then multiply by 52 weeks in a year. For example, a nurse earning $45 per hour would have an annual gross of $45 × 38 × 52 = $88,920. This figure is before tax, the Medicare levy, and superannuation.

### The Role of the National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual workers receive a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. However, most nurses are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for the health industry. The figures here are estimates and may differ from your actual award rate. The Queensland full-time ordinary time average weekly earnings, as reported by the Australian Bureau of Statistics for May 2026, is $2,039.70 per week. This is an average across all industries in Queensland, not a median for a specific job like a nurse. Your actual nurse salary QLD will depend on your classification, experience, and any allowances.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Breakdown

To see your pay on a fortnightly basis, simply multiply your weekly gross by two. Using the $45 per hour example, weekly gross is $45 × 38 = $1,710, so fortnightly gross is $3,420. This can help you budget and compare with salary offers that are quoted per fortnight. Remember that tax is withheld each pay period, so your bank deposit will be less.

### Estimating Tax and Medicare Levy on Your Annual Figure

Once you have your annual gross, you can estimate the tax you will pay using the 2026–27 resident tax rates. The first $18,200 is tax-free. Then:
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. For a nurse earning $88,920 annually, the tax would be approximately:
- $0 on first $18,200
- 15% on $26,800 ($18,201 to $45,000) = $4,020
- 30% on $43,920 ($45,001 to $88,920) = $13,176
Total tax = $17,196. Medicare levy at 2% = $1,778.40. Total deductions = $18,974.40, leaving an estimated take-home pay of $69,945.60 per year. This is a rough estimate; your actual tax may vary due to offsets, deductions, or the Medicare levy surcharge. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for more details.

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Superannuation is not included in your annual gross figure. Your employer must pay an additional 12% of your ordinary time earnings into your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For the $88,920 annual gross, that is an extra $10,670.40 per year. This is separate from your salary and is not subject to income tax until you withdraw it in retirement. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Casual Loading and Other Considerations

If you are a casual nurse, your hourly rate typically includes a 25% loading in lieu of paid leave. The base rate for a casual is higher than the permanent rate. When using the timesheet on this site, you can check a box to add 25% casual loading on top of your base hourly rate. Do not enter a rate that already includes the loading. For award-covered nurses, the loading is often built into the award rate. Always check your specific award or agreement.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detailed reference tables, see our [reference tables](/data) page. To start calculating your own figures, visit [the timesheet](/) and enter your base hourly rate.
